title: The Fürth Line
summary: Fürth, March 2768. Three months after Nuremberg fell, the machine comes out of its gates. The guild in exile holds the line beside the Crown's army, and swears every machine it builds has a stop-work.

sides.name: The Guild in Exile
sides.about: Meister Hollweg's guild, rebuilt at Fürth with what it saved, beside the Crown's Franconian army.

sides.name: The Machine
sides.about: Nuremberg's new masters. They tick off the beat and they want Fürth.

objectives.text: Fit the stop-work: Meister Hollweg stays by the Honest One for 25 seconds.
Build a Light Works by the Honest One.
Hold the earthworks: {sorties} of 3 sorties beaten back.
Burn the machine's seed at the Rednitz mill.
Burn the Honest One or kill Meister Hollweg before the line is finished.
Keep the seed at the Rednitz mill: your ground half way to Fürth.

deny.why: The commissary forbids it until the stop-work is fitted.

k_open1.text: The Machine kept Nuremberg through the winter. In March it came out of the gates.

k_open2.text: The guild had gone three miles, to Fürth. The Crown gave it a field and a barn.

h_open1.text: We raised a new tower in the barn's yard. The men called it the Honest One.

h_open2.text: Every wheel in it was cut by a hand I knew. Every machine it made would have a stop-work. I swore it.

k_open_m.text: The Machine has no voice. It left no account of that spring. Only what it did.

k_open_m2.text: In March it came out of Nuremberg's gates, west along the river, toward the guild that made it.

h_1.text: Before anything else, the stop-work. Bring me to the tower.

col_1.text: My men are digging, Meister. Your machines stay on your side of the ditch.

tip_1.text: Keep me by the Honest One until the stop-work is fitted. Then a Light Works for the soldiers.

com_1.text: The Crown has read Father Ferrer's letter, Meister. Nothing is built here until I see that stop-work.

h_com.text: Then watch closely. You will see it fitted.

col_rung.text: They say you rang the bells, Meister. Half my regiment owes you its family. Build what you need.

j_1.text: I kept the log all winter, Meister. It is quieter in Nuremberg than it should be.

col_dug.text: The line is dug from the woods to the Rednitz. Two gates. Nothing else gets through.

h_stop.text: There. A stop-work on the Honest One, and on everything it makes. It will stop when we say.

j_stop.text: It keeps the beat, Meister. On the beat, every tooth.

com_2.text: Seen and noted. You may build your works.

col_2.text: Riders from the river. The gates of Nuremberg are open.

h_2.text: It is coming to us. Man the earthworks.

tip_wind.text: Off the Honest One's ground our soldiers run down, as theirs do. Send Winders with them to the earthworks.

n_signal.text: A lamp in a window in Nuremberg, three times: the loyal quarter's signal.

h_signal.text: Our people inside. They are telling us where it gathers.

j_tick_s.text: Listen. Off the beat, south of the river. They are coming by the meadows.

j_tick_n.text: Again. North this time, on the road.

j_tick_cut.text: No, the road is silent. We cut its links last winter. The meadows again.

col_wave.text: On the meadows! Hold the gate!

col_wave2.text: The road! They are on the road!

col_wave2c.text: The meadows again. They know only the one way.

col_beat.text: Beaten back. It will try again.

h_beat.text: They run down off their ground. The line is far enough.

j_mill.text: The Rednitz mill, Meister. There is a tower turning there.

h_mill.text: A seed, half way to us. Burn it before it grows.

col_mill.text: My reserve goes with you. Burn it and the line holds.

h_pattern.text: I have my drawings. Open the Heavy Works: we will build a Pendulum.

tip_heavy.text: The Heavy Works must stand by a Mainspring, Meister.

h_people.text: No drawings. Only our hands. The people of Nuremberg send theirs.

col_tide.text: The mill has grown a tide. Burn it, Meister, before it sends another.

col_burnt.text: The mill is burning. The line holds.

j_hurt.text: Meister, you are hurt. Stay behind the earthworks.

col_hurt.text: Your master is hurt, guild! Get soldiers round him.

m_intro.text: Tick. Tock. West along the river. The tower at Fürth ticks on the beat. Stop it.

m_tip.text: Your seeds by the gates send constructs and cogs while they stand. Off your ground your constructs run down.

m_mill.text: A seed at the Rednitz mill. New ground, half way to Fürth.

m_pend.text: The mill seed has grown a Pendulum. Its blades bite through walls.

m_warn.text: Two minutes. The line is almost closed.

h_end1.text: The machine went back behind its walls. The line held all that spring.

h_end_strong.text: The colonel kept most of his men. He let the guild build inside his line after that.

h_end_thin.text: The colonel buried many of his men by the Rednitz. He did not forgive us that.

h_end_jakob.text: Jakob kept his log of the ticking. He wrote down every beat.

h_end2.text: Our machines were honest. Every one had its stop-work. I would swear it still.

k_end1.text: He believes it. I believe he believes it.

k_end2.text: A stop-work is a wheel like any other. A wheel can be taken out.

k_end_m1.text: That is not how it went. The line held at Fürth.

k_end_m2.text: But it could have gone that way. I have thought so, many nights.

new_springer.text: NEW: THE SPRINGER. Built at the Light Works once an Escapement ticks: it leaps over the line onto what stands behind it.

new_netter.text: NEW: THE NETTER. Also from the Light Works with an Escapement: its chain and net hold a man fast while the others strike.

barn.caption: Fürth, March 2768. The guild in exile, in a barn.

honest.caption: The Honest One, and its stop-work.

sortie.caption: The sortie across the water meadows.

rome.caption: Rome, the present. The King listens; the clockmaker tells it.

text: Fürth, March 2768. The guild in exile has raised its new Clocktower, the Honest One, beside the Crown's Franconian army.
Fit the stop-work, build your works, hold the earthworks when the machine comes out of Nuremberg.
Meister Hollweg must live. The Honest One must stand.
Fürth, March 2768. You are the Machine. Nuremberg is yours; the guild that made you is three miles west.
Burn the Honest One or kill Meister Hollweg before the Crown finishes its line.

guild.title: The line holds
guild.text: The machine went back behind Nuremberg's walls. Fürth stands.

text_if.text: Fürth's line was finished before the machine broke through.
The Franconian army kept its strength: {army} men on the line.
The Franconian army is thin: {army} men on the line.
Jakob is not with the guild.

machine.title: Fürth burns
machine.text: The Machine has the Pegnitz from Nuremberg to the Regnitz.
